questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: A popular meal of seafood and steak
How to find the cheapest prices online
Why shops are closing on the high street
People filling online shopping baskets but not paying
questions.why: Rob explains 'surf and turf' as putting things in a virtual basket but not completing the purchase.

questions.q: How does Neil misunderstand 'surf and turf' at first?
options: He thinks it's a water sport
He thinks Rob means a meal of lobster and steak
He thinks it's a type of garden
He thinks it's the name of a new shopping website
questions.why: Neil talks about 'some lobster, a juicy steak', and Rob says he's got the wrong end of the stick.

questions.q: According to the research, how many people abandoned an online basket in the last year?
options: About 40%
About 18%
About 70%
About 10%
questions.why: Rob says approximately 40% of people have abandoned an online shopping basket in the last year.

questions.q: What does Rob think about the figure of 18 billion pounds of lost sales?
options: It is too low
It is exactly right
He doubts it, as people don't plan to buy everything
He thinks the shops should get all of that money back from customers
questions.why: Rob says he's sceptical, because 'we don't always intend to buy everything we put in our baskets'.

questions.q: Why does Neil agree that some of the money was never really lost?
options: Some people buy the same things in another shop
Most people come back the next day and buy everything
Shops have insurance
People buy the items by phone
questions.why: Neil says you might check another store for cheaper items, so some money would have gone to other stores.

questions.q: Which of these is a reason for not finishing a purchase that Rob and Neil mention?
options: The website is too colourful
The items they want are often out of stock
The shop is closed
High delivery costs or complicated payment
questions.why: Rob mentions high delivery costs or paying being very complicated, and Neil agrees.

questions.q: What did retail expert Clare Bailey find about over 70% of retailers?
options: They had stopped selling online
They hadn't improved their payment process in two years
They charged their customers far too much for delivery
They had too few customers
questions.why: She says over 70% 'hadn't invested in the payment process in the last two years'.

questions.q: What mistake does Clare Bailey suggest retailers make?
options: They spend far too much money on advertising and not enough on products
They don't have enough products
They invest in getting us to the checkout, but not in it
They make their websites too slow
questions.why: She says they invested in getting us to that page 'and then they fell foul'.
